forensic_metrics.financial: Managed $10k+ rapid prototyping budget for high-pressure trade show build [1], [2]; Negotiated short-run fab costs (e.g., $164.95/cover) [3].
forensic_metrics.process: Reduced complex sheet metal fabrication cycle to 9 days [4], [5]; Standardized 100% of assembly hardware to 4-40 spec to eliminate line-down risks [6].
forensic_metrics.governance: Orchestrated parallel workstreams between sheet metal (E-M Solutions) and model shops (Sputnik) under a high-velocity 'War Room' cadence [7].

forensic_summary.trigger: The 'Elmer' main board relied on an aluminum heat spreader requiring a 'dead nuts flat' chassis for thermal conduction, a tolerance impossibility for sheet metal [8], [9]. Simultaneously, a 'screw-up' on the prototype build mixed metric and SAE hardware [6].
forensic_summary.intervention: Norris ('The Architect') rejected the 'Bastard Box' concept [10] and executed a custom chassis design removing perforation under the PCB for mass conduction [11]. He enforced a strict 4-40 UNC hardware standardization for the 'Zeus' revision [6].
forensic_summary.result: Delivery of 5 functional server enclosures and 12 nodes for Western Cable Show and CES 2001 on a compressed 9-day fabrication cycle with zero thermal failures [4], [5].

war_stories.label: The Dead Nuts Flat Fallacy
war_stories.description: Removed perforation under heat spreader to maximize conductive mass, rejecting the impossible flatness requirement [8], [11].

war_stories.label: The Hardware Screw-Up
war_stories.description: Purged mixed metric/SAE hardware, standardizing to 4-40 UNC to prevent assembly line stoppages [8], [6].

war_stories.label: The Bastard Box Pivot
war_stories.description: Killed the ill-defined 'Bastard Box' concept to focus resources on refining the Elmer/Zeus chassis for the hard deadline [12], [10].

isomorphics.label: Standardization
isomorphics.hardware_point: Mixed metric/SAE fasteners cause assembly friction and cross-threading.
isomorphics.software_point: Inconsistent dependency versions cause build failures ('Dependency Hell').
isomorphics.principle: Reducing component entropy increases system yield.
